title: VLSI CAD Timing Intern - Applied AI
description: NVIDIA has continuously reinvented itself over two decades. Our invention of the GPU in 1999 sparked the growth of the PC gaming market, redefined modern computer graphics, and revolutionized parallel computing. More recently, GPU deep learning ignited modern AI — the next era of computing. NVIDIA is a “learning machine” that constantly evolves by adapting to new opportunities that are hard to resolve, that only we can seek, and that matter to the world. This is our life’s work, to amplify human inventiveness and intelligence. We are looking for a VLSI CAD Timing Intern focused on Applied AI to lead end-to-end solution development — spanning data generation, model training, orchestration, and agentic automation — for timing and constraint analysis workflows. You will be part of a cross-disciplinary team building intelligent systems that learn from sign-off data, reason across flows, and assist engineers in achieving faster and more predictable closure. What You’ll Be Doing: Learn and support static timing analysis (STA) flows using industry tools like PrimeTime and Tempus for advanced ASIC designs. Help develop and automate timing, constraints, and QoR validation flows using scripting and data-driven methods. Assist with analyzing timing reports, constraints, and design data across corners and modes to improve closure predictability. Collaborate with CAD, physical design, and methodology engineers on timing sign-off strategies and best practices. Contribute to early AI- or analytics-assisted approaches for timing analysis, constraint checking, or flow optimization. Explore how physical effects (e.g., IR drop, crosstalk, aging, thermal impact) influence timing and design decisions. What we need to see: Currently pursuing a Master’s or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. Coursework or academic knowledge in VLSI/ASIC design, digital circuits, or computer architecture. Exposure to applying agentic AI to back-end VLSI tasks (e.g., floorplanning, timing closure, or physical verification). Familiarity with the basics of static timing analysis, constraints, or digital design flows. Knowledge in scripting or programming (Python preferred). Comfort working with data, reports, and technical problem-solving in complex systems. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Academic projects, research, or internships related to VLSI, physical design, STA, or EDA tools. Exposure to TCL. Exposure to machine learning, data analysis, or AI concepts applied to engineering problems. Experience automating workflows, analyzing large datasets, or contributing to technical tools or open-source projects. NVIDIA is widely considered one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We employ some of the most forward-thinking and talented people in the world. Are you passionate about joining our life work to amplify human creativity and intelligence? If you are creative, collaborative, and have a real passion for design methodology and automation, we want to hear from you. Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay based on the position, your location, year in school, degree, and experience. The hourly rate for our interns is 20 USD - 71 USD. You will also be eligible for Intern benefits . ​ Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 2, 2026. This posting is for an existing vacancy. NVIDIA uses AI tools in its recruiting processes. NVIDIA is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment and proud to be an equal opportunity employer. As we highly value diversity in our current and future employees, we do not discriminate (including in our hiring and promotion practices) on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: ASIC Design Verification Internship (16 Month Coop - Summer 2027) Kanata, Canada Category: Interns/Temp Posted: 10/28/2026 Job ID: 19523
description: We Are Drive technology innovations that shape the way we live and connect. Our technology drives the Era of Pervasive Intelligence, where smart tech and AI are seamlessly woven into daily life. From self-driving cars and health-monitoring smartwatches to renewable energy systems that efficiently distribute clean power, Synopsys creates high-performance silicon chips that help build a healthier, safer, and more sustainable world. Internship Experience At Synopsys, interns dive into real-world projects, gaining hands-on experience while collaborating with our passionate teams worldwide - and having fun in the process! You'll have the freedom to share your ideas, unleash your creativity, and explore your interests. This is your opportunity to bring your solutions to life and work with cutting-edge technology that shapes not only the future of innovation but also your own career path. Join us and start shaping your future today! Mission Statement: Our mission is to fuel today's innovations and spark tomorrow's creativity. Together, we embrace a growth mindset, empower one another, and collaborate to achieve our shared goals. What You'll Be Doing: • Testbench Development: Work within a UVM (Universal Verification Methodology) testbench to verify SerDes ASIC RTL designs, gaining practical exposure to industry-standard verification frameworks. • Protocol & Architecture Mastery: Develop in-depth knowledge of the PCIe protocol and the internal architecture of SerDes ASIC chips, understanding how cutting-edge hardware designs come to life. • Advanced DV Methodology: Learn and apply comprehensive Design Verification (DV) concepts, including the Register Abstraction Layer (RAL), UVM phases, UVM objects, drivers, monitors, and scoreboards. • Debugging & Analysis: Perform wave analysis and debug complex designs using industry-standard Synopsys tools such as Verdi, building critical problem-solving skills. • Collaborative Learning: Work closely with senior engineers, participating in design reviews and team discussions to accelerate your professional growth and technical expertise. title: Systems Software Engineer Intern
description: Please Note: To provide the best candidate experience amidst our high application volumes, each candidate is limited to 10 applications across all open jobs within a 6-month period. Advancing the World’s Technology Together Our technology solutions power the tools you use every day--including smartphones, electric vehicles, hyperscale data centers, IoT devices, and so much more. Here, you’ll have an opportunity to be part of a global leader whose innovative designs are pushing the boundaries of what’s possible and powering the future. We believe innovation and growth are driven by an inclusive culture and a diverse workforce. We’re dedicated to empowering people to be their true selves. Together, we’re building a better tomorrow for our employees, customers, partners, and communities. What You’ll Learn Project Overview: Develop systems software for memory and storage pools that support reinforcement-learning post-training of large language models Skills You’ll Learn: Core Linux kernel memory management for virtual machines How to modify the Linux kernel memory/storage management subsystem Contributing to the largest open source project in the world Understand how open-source SW impacts Samsung business Collaborating across team, Samsung, and industry What You’ll Do The Samsung Global Ecosystem Team (GOST) is seeking an intern to develop systems software for memory and storage pools that support reinforcement-learning post-training of large language models. The work will examine how rollout generation, reward evaluation, policy updates, and checkpoint recovery use shared resources. You will build a focused prototype using fabric-attached memory and SSD pool, and measure its effect on training progress, memory pressure, and recovery time. GOST consists of a geographically distributed group of engineers making high impact contributions both in software and leadership to open ecosystems such as the Linux kernel and QEMU. This work supports Samsung’s latest storage and memory technologies. As an intern, you will contribute to the SW ecosystem R&D efforts targeting Samsung’s latest memory and storage technologies globally through distributed open-source projects. The goal of the internship is to deliver a working memory-to-storage data path, a live RL post-training demonstration, and a measured explanation of when pooling improves training efficiency or recoverability. Location: Daily onsite presence at our San Jose headquarters in alignment with our Flexible Work policy Reports to: Principal Engineer Responsibilities Profile the RL post-training loop to identify memory-capacity limits, data-transfer overhead, storage stalls, and GPU idle time. Develop one runtime feature that coordinates bounded memory staging, asynchronous storage writes, prefetching, or capacity allocation across workers. Integrate the feature with an existing RL framework using its training and checkpoint interfaces. Preserve snapshot consistency, policy-version provenance, buffer ownership, and durable checkpoint publication during asynchronous operations. Compare memory-only, storage-only, and combined pool configurations using training throughput, GPU-hours, local-memory usage, and restart performance. Deliver correctness tests, reproducible experiments, design documentation, and code suitable for review and potential open-source contribution. Find the resource management issue on post-RL workload and resolve the issue in host OS. Complete other responsibilities as assigned. Complete other responsibilities as assigned. What You Bring Pursuing Masters, or PhD in Computer Science Must have at least 1 academic quarter/semester remaining Programming experience in C, C++, or Rust, with Python or shell scripting for experiments and automation. Understanding of operating systems, memory management, concurrency, and computer architecture. Experience developing and debugging on Linux, using Git, and communicating technical results—coursework and research projects count. CXL, NUMA, Device-DAX, mmap, shared-memory programming, or memory allocators, preferred GPU programming, CUDA, DMA, or profiling memory and data-transfer performance, preferred Distributed systems, cache management, vllm, sglang, LLM inference, or open-source development, preferred You’re inclusive, adapting your style to the situation and diverse global norms of our people. An avid learner, you approach challenges with curiosity and resilience, seeking data to help build understanding. You’re collaborative, building relationships, humbly offering support and openly welcoming approaches. Innovative and creative, you proactively explore new ideas and adapt quickly to change. What We Offer The pay range below is for all roles at this level across all US locations and functions. Pay within this range varies by work location and may also depend on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This is in addition to our diverse package of benefits centered around the wellbeing of our employees and their loved ones. In addition to the usual Medical/Dental/Vision, our inclusive rewards plan empowers our people to care for their whole selves. An investment in your future is an investment in ours. Relocation Support Live 50+ miles away from your new office? No worries! We'll provide a stipend to help support your move. Housing Stipend Signing a lease on a new place for your summer internship? We'll help you pay your way with a monthly stipend. Give Back With a charitable giving match and frequent opportunities to get involved, we take an active role in supporting the community. Prioritize Emotional Wellness With on-demand apps and paid therapy sessions, you’ll have support no matter where you are. Stay Fit Eating well and being active are important parts of a healthy life. Our onsite Café and gym, plus virtual classes, make it easier. Embrace Flexibility Benefits are best when you have the space to use them. That’s why we facilitate a flexible environment so you can find the right balance for you. title: AI Systems Software Engineer Intern
description: NVIDIA is looking for an AI Systems Software Engineering Intern to apply AI agents, machine learning, and performance engineering to compilers and developer tools. You will work with compiler and AI engineers on a scoped project involving code, compiler and performance feedback, experiments, and optimization. Depending on your background and interests, the work may focus on agentic workflows, learned models, performance analysis, or AI-enabled developer tools. Experience in every area is not expected. What you’ll be doing: Build AI-agent workflows that interact with code, compilers, benchmarks, performance tools, and engineering systems. Develop tools that help agents collect data, run experiments, analyze compiler and performance feedback, identify optimization opportunities, and recommend next steps. Explore data-driven approaches for compiler optimization, performance prediction, decision support, and workflow automation. Build reliable interfaces between AI agents and compiler or developer-tool infrastructure. Prototype improvements to compiler flows, optimization tools, experimentation systems, or developer workflows. Work with compiler, architecture, AI, and performance engineers to evaluate ideas on representative workloads. Measure correctness, runtime performance, compile time, reliability, and other relevant outcomes. Document the design, experiments, results, limitations, and next steps. What we need to see: Pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Strong programming skills in Python, C, C++, or a similar language. Solid foundations in data structures, algorithms, software engineering, and quantitative problem solving. Coursework, research, or project experience in one or more of these areas: AI, machine learning, AI agents, compilers, programming languages, systems, performance engineering, optimization, or developer tools. Ability to design experiments, analyze results, investigate technical problems, and communicate findings clearly. Interest in learning across AI, compiler, performance, and systems boundaries. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Experience building AI agents, LLM applications, evaluation systems, coding workflows, or developer tools. Experience with LLVM, MLIR, compiler optimization passes, code generation, domain-specific languages, or compiler infrastructure. Familiarity with GPU architecture, CUDA, GPU programming, or performance optimization. Hands-on experience with reinforcement learning, evolutionary algorithms, predictive modeling, ranking, search, or high-dimensional data analysis. Research, internships, open-source contributions, or personal projects that measure runtime, compile time, resource use, code quality, or developer productivity. Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay based on the position, your location, year in school, degree, and experience. The hourly rate for our interns is 20 USD - 71 USD. You will also be eligible for Intern benefits . ​ Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 2, 2026. This posting is for an existing vacancy. title: Swift Runtime Engineer Intern - Swift Runtimes
description: The Swift Runtimes team at Apple is looking for an intern to contribute to our work on the Swift language runtime libraries. This position provides the opportunity to work with our world-class runtime engineers on code whose performance has an impact both across Apple's product range and in the wider Swift community. Description You will contribute to the evolution and development of the cross-platform runtime libraries that underpin the Swift programming language itself, and will have a chance to learn about the lowest level aspects of the runtime environment for a sophisticated modern programming language. As a member of the Swift Open Source community, you will contribute code publicly to the Swift project repositories on Github, and will have access to technical guidance, code reviews and mentorship from other community members to help you grow and get valuable experience contributing to a large, popular, Open Source project. The position is based on-site at Apple's London campus. We are looking for candidates with strong development skills and an interest in the low-level runtime aspects of programming languages. Minimum qualifications Interest in low-level systems programming Practical experience with C++ Basic knowledge of Swift Strong communication and teamwork skills Preferred qualifications Practical experience with Swift Familiarity with x86-64 and/or Arm64 assembly language Experience contributing to Open Source projects Interest in compilers and programming languages Development experience on multiple platforms

title: Internship - Data Engineering
description: Company Description WD is building the infrastructure behind the AI-driven data economy. As AI scales, so does data. Every interaction, every model, every system generates data that must be stored, managed, and made accessible over time. That’s where we come in. We combine deep engineering expertise with global-scale manufacturing to deliver the storage systems that make AI possible, powering hyperscale data centers, cloud platforms, and enterprise infrastructure worldwide. This isn’t theoretical work. It’s real systems, at real scale, people solving some of the hardest challenges in technology today. We’re looking for people who want to build, solve, and operate at that level. Join us and let’s shape the future of data. Job Description We are looking for a Data Engineering Intern  to support our engineering operations team. This role covers applied work across schema design, data ingestion, API interfaces, template generation logic, and reporting dashboards — with exposure to multiple data types including relational, time-series, and vector/knowledge data. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Assist in database schema design and documentation for an automation system supporting engineering test operations. Develop and maintain ETL pipelines for data ingestion and transformation workflows. Build basic API interfaces for data access and integration with engineering platforms and systems Implement template parameter mapping and generation logic using templating frameworks. Support reporting and dashboarding development for engineering and operational metrics. Perform data quality checks and validation across structured and unstructured data sources. Maintain clear documentation for pipelines, schemas, and workflows. Participate in code reviews and maintain clean, well-documented code. This position is part of our Early Career program at WD. Our Early Career program is designed to support individuals beginning their professional career by providing the foundational training through a structured onboarding, mentorship, and development curriculum. Qualifications REQUIRED Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, Data Science, or a related field. Expected internship onboarding/start date: Early 2027. SKILLS Solid foundation in SQL and relational database concepts. Experience with Python for data handling and transformation (pandas / polars a plus). Familiarity with REST API concepts — consuming endpoints and mapping data. Basic understanding of ETL pipeline design and data ingestion workflows. Experience with templating frameworks or code generation tools.
